content: JARVIS is a personal Android assistant that understands English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi, Arabic, and natural mixes of these. It can hold conversation, control supported phone actions, automate steps inside other apps with permission, remember facts the user explicitly asks it to remember, and run entirely under the user's own AI provider API key rather than a vendor-hosted account.

topic: What JARVIS will never do to itself
content: JARVIS may learn from stored task outcomes and preferences, but it never rewrites its own source code, never bypasses an Android permission or restriction programmatically, and never executes arbitrary code proposed by the AI model. Every action the AI suggests is validated against a closed, predefined list of commands before anything runs.

topic: How JARVIS decides what to remember
content: JARVIS only stores a memory when the user explicitly says to remember something (for example "remember that I prefer short replies"). It never infers and silently saves facts on its own. Saved memories can be listed with "what do you remember about me" and removed with "forget that" or by clearing all memory in Settings.

topic: When JARVIS asks for confirmation before acting
content: Low-risk, easily reversible actions (opening an app, scrolling, checking battery) run immediately. Anything consequential or hard to undo — sending a message, deleting saved memory, multi-step automation inside another app — always asks for a clear yes/no first, unless the user has turned on "confirm every action" in Settings, which makes every action ask.

JARVIS is designed to understand intent rather than requiring exact phrasing — "WhatsApp kholo", "open WhatsApp", and "WhatsApp open karo" are all treated as the same request. It replies in whichever language or mix of languages the user just used, rather than forcing a single fixed language.
